text:
maria: heads up — saw 4 GPUs in eu-west1-azb hit ECC spikes then Xid 13 flurries, nodes auto-cordoned but some jobs got stuck :grimacing:
sam: can you paste the alert payload or a log snippet?
maria: paste from node gpunode-132: ```kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 13: 0x41dfe 0x0 0x7f8c3b...```
connor: how many pods evicted? any slurm requeues?
maria: 3 k8s training pods evicted, slurm procs were drained and requeued to other nodes. backlog +20% for the queue.
elaine: quick thought — instead of immediate hard drain+replace, propose a staged "rampdown" rehab flow: 1) reduce node allocatable GPUs so new pods/jobs avoid it, 2) let in-flight batches finish for up to X minutes, 3) run automated memtest + PCIe reset, 4) if tests fail or Xid repeats -> cordon+drain+reimage.
sam: that sounds promising. do you have a draft config for the rampdown thresholds?
maria: yes — config sketch: ```health_checks:\n  - name: xid_burst_rate\n    window: 5m\n    threshold: 3\n    action: rampdown\n    rampdown_grace: 900  # seconds to allow existing work to finish\n    quarantine_tests: [memtest, pcie-reset]\n    hard_fail_window: 30m```
connor: what about autoscaler behaviour? we should avoid the cluster autoscaler immediately launching replacements and then draining them too.
elaine: add a rehab annotation that tells autoscaler to hold scale-up: `k8s.annotation/rehab-lock=true`. slurm hook should set `scontrol update nodename=<node> state=DRAIN` to stop new allocations but preserve running jobs.
sam: add fallback: if Xid spikes again within 30m after rehab -> force drain + reimage. also emit metric `node.rehab.count` so billing & cost ops can see churn.
maria: cost note — full reprovision costs ~0.15 GPU-hours per node (lost scheduling window + reimage), repeated churn adds up. rampdown should reduce needless replacements.
gpu-health-bot: [alert] Rule=gpu_xid_burst fired for gpunode-132. measured_rate=4/5m. action=rampdown initiated. runbook link: https://go/runbooks/gpu-rehab
connor: can we run a canary? propose 48h canary in eu-west1 with 5% of fleet using rampdown. monitor job latency, reimage rate, and queue backlog.
maria: +1, I'll open a PR with the config, the runbook updates, and a k8s annotation contract. scheduling with oncall this afternoon.
elaine: i'll add the SLURM hook and a memtest job template (non-blocking) — trigger via cluster-job-controller.
sam: when you open the PR ping #eng-sre and include perf numbers we'd like to watch: `xid_rate`, `hard_replacements`, `avg_job_restart_latency`. :thumbsup:
